title: Get Specs Health
description: The `GetSpecsHealth` use case provides a lightweight summary of the project's specification validation status. By aggregating overall counts and returning only the failing or warned specifications in a consolidated format, it avoids transferring large lists of successful validations, optimizing payload sizes for clients.
context: The `GetSpecsHealth` use case provides a lightweight summary of the project's specification validation status. By aggregating overall counts and returning only the failing or warned specifications in a consolidated format, it avoids transferring large lists of successful validations, optimizing payload sizes for clients.

rules:
The `GetSpecsHealth` usecase MUST invoke `ValidateSpecs.execute()` internally.
The resulting `GetSpecsHealthResult` SHALL exclude specifications that passed cleanly (0 failures, 0 warnings). It SHALL only report validation results for specifications that failed to validate cleanly (meaning `passed === false` or `warnings.length > 0`).

The resulting `GetSpecsHealthResult` SHALL aggregate overall validation statistics across the project:

- `totalSpecs`: The total number of specs validated.
- `passed`: The number of specs that passed cleanly (0 failures, 0 warnings).
- `failed`: The number of specs that failed validation (having one or more failures).
- `warned`: The number of specs that contain warnings but no failures.

These states SHALL be mutually exclusive, satisfying the invariant:
$$\text{totalSpecs} = \text{passed} + \text{failed} + \text{warned}$$

For each spec that failed or has warnings, its diagnostics SHALL be consolidated into a single object under the `issues` array. Each entry in `issues` SHALL contain:

- `spec`: The canonical spec path.
- `passed`: A boolean indicating if the spec has no failures (true if it has only warnings, false if it has failures).
- `failures`: The array of validation failures.
- `warnings`: The array of validation warnings.
The `GetSpecsHealth` usecase SHALL support an optional `workspace` filter in its input, delegating this filter directly to the underlying `ValidateSpecs` execution.

scenarios.name: Exclude clean specs from issues list
given: a workspace containing both clean specs and specs with validation errors or warnings
then: the returning issues array SHALL NOT contain any entries for specs that passed cleanly
AND the issues array SHALL contain entries for specs with errors or warnings

scenarios.name: Aggregate overall counts
given: a workspace with 5 specs: 2 clean, 2 with errors, and 1 with only warnings

scenarios.name: Single issue entry per spec containing both failures and warnings
given: a spec that has 1 local validation failure and 1 validation warning
then: the spec SHALL appear exactly once in the issues array
AND its passed property SHALL be false
AND its failures array SHALL contain the failure detail object
AND its warnings array SHALL contain the warning detail object

scenarios.name: Filter validation by workspace
then: only specs belonging to the core workspace are validated and counted
AND statistics represent the core workspace only
